subject: On-prem georouting & circuitization — EU/APAC SLA exceptions
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@eurocloud-sys.eu>

Subject: Initial: EU/APAC on-prem circuitization and SLA exception questions

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is the provider-side topology we discussed (network-diagram_v2.png) — high level circuit layout between EuroCloud peering points in Frankfurt and our APAC edge POPs. Before we proceed to a formal Design Review, two things we need clarity on from Redwood: 

1) Control-plane residency during failover: if we fail traffic from EU -> APAC (planned or automated), is the control plane connection for the private deployment allowed to cross regions for a bounded window (we typically expect <30 minutes)? Our security team flagged this as an "SLA exception" that needs an approved justification.

2) Cold vs warm standby expectations: the diagram assumes cold standby in APAC (VPC to be rehydrated on demand). Redwood asked for a warm standby config for lower RTOs; we need to know what minimum RTO/RPO Redwood requires to consider the system "compliant" with your residency guarantees.

We have a couple of constraints on our side: cross-border packet inspection by our local partner must remain inside APAC for 95% of the traffic post-cutover, and the procurement team will only accept up to two SLA exception windows per quarter.

Can you confirm the operational fallback sequence you expect (control-plane kept local vs allowed to transit), and whether Redwood can commit to an APAC warm standby profile for 6x9s SLA?

If it helps, Kai (cc'd offline) can provide measured latencies on the peering links.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: Initial: EU/APAC on-prem circuitization and SLA exception questions

Anna — thanks for the diagram and the clear constraints. High level answers below, plus a suggested next step (short DR sync).

- Control-plane residency during failover: Redwood's default position is that control-plane traffic for Private deployments remains pinned to the region declared by the customer. For emergency automated failovers where compute shifts to another region, we do allow a temporary control-plane tunnel across regions for up to 45 minutes while we perform verification and state reconciliation. That exception is auditable and can be constrained by a policy (we can set a hard 30-minute limit if you prefer).

- Warm vs cold standby: Warm standby in APAC (pre-provisioned VPC with hot KV cache priming) is the recommended approach if you need RTO under 5 minutes. Cold standby (on-demand provisioning) usually yields RTOs in the 20–60 minute range depending on image pull times and network attach. For a 6x9s SLA (99.9999) the platform-level requirement is warm standby with periodic cache syncs and an automated health-gated failover.

Operational fallback sequence (proposed):
1) Prefail detection -> redirect read-only to warm standby (APAC) if configured.
2) If primary recovery fails within configured window, promote warm standby and rotate KMS keys scoped to APAC.
3) Keep control-plane tunnel active for verification (default 45m, configurable to 30m) and emit audit event with justification.
4) Post-cutover, revert control-plane endpoints to local-only as soon as state is consistent.

Action items: 
- Laura, Marcus: can you confirm whether the procurement/legal side will accept a short (<=45m) control-plane transit exception with an auditable justification?
- Anna: would you accept a hard 30-minute window if EuroCloud policy requires it?

I can pull in our security/compliance SME to the DR call if you want an on-record justification for audit. Suggested time for a 40-minute design review: Mon Apr 12 09:00 CEST / Apr 12 16:00 JST.

—
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial: EU/APAC on-prem circuitization and SLA exception questions

Olga / Anna — quick notes from the risk and governance side after reviewing the topology. Forwarding the earlier note from Olga for context.

Key risks: 
- KMS locality: If we rotate keys during failover and KMS is in EU, we must ensure key material does not egress to APAC systems. Our preferred pattern is: replicate encrypted blobs and use a regional KMS key in APAC for runtime decryption; control-plane tunnel used for orchestration signals only and not for key material.
- Audit trail: procurement will require a pre-approved runbook listing the triggers for a control-plane transit exception (preferred: binary triggers only — datacenter outage, widespread packet loss >X%, scheduled DR exercise).

Operational ask: we have an internal SOP for warm standby activation; attaching a trimmed version that specifies smoke tests and manual gating steps (sop-warm-standby.pdf). If EuroCloud needs a 30-minute hard window, we should also add a compensated control — e.g., automated snapshot verification to speed up reversion.

On standby sizing: warm standby with KV priming at 20% of steady-state request rate looks sufficient to meet an RTO <5m for user-facing generation routes. Background batch workloads will need separate capacity planning.

I'll join the proposed DR call and will bring the compliance SME. Marcus, can you run a quick feasibility check on the warm standby storage replication costs and note any procurement implications?

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Laura / Olga — thanks for the clear responses and the SOP. Procurement and security have reviewed the proposal and are comfortable with the following compromise: 

- Control-plane transit exception: allowable up to 30 minutes, but must be accompanied by an automated audit event and a post-incident report with root-cause analysis. Two exception windows per quarter max.
- Warm standby: EuroCloud will accept Redwood's warm standby profile for RTO <5m for generation routes. We will scope batch workloads separately.

We can take the DR call on Apr 12 as proposed. Kai will join from APAC and will bring measured link stats. Please include calendar invite link and a short agenda (20m design + 20m compliance discussion).

Thanks,
